issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

I want to run a `cc_binary` under `valgrind`. I get `valgrind` through an `http_archive`, so I call bazel like this:

```
bazel run --run_under=@valgrind//:valgrind //path/to/my/binary
```
Now, `valgrind` is composed of a `wrapper` plus some data:

```
sh_binary(
    name = "valgrind",
    srcs = [":wrapper"],
    data = glob([
        "usr/bin/*",
        "usr/lib/**/*",
        "usr/libexec/**/*",
    ]),
)
```

The problem is that when running the above line, Bazel doesn't pull the `data` into the sandbox (`.runfiles` folder). I.e. the `wrapper` exists, but not the `data` it needs, so it complains about files not being found.

However, if I change my `cc_binary` into a `cc_test`, it works just fine.

Why is this happening? Is this expected?

### Feature requests: what underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?

I want to be able to use tools that rely on `data` for the `--run_under` command.

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

This issue is very similar to this one: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7656. I believe the problem can easily be reproduced by adding some `data` to the `sh_binary` tool that is used for `--run_under`.

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

Ubuntu 18.04.

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

release 5.0.0-pre.20210907.1

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

This issue, which is similar but seems to have been fixed: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7656

issue.body:
### Description of the bug:


`--run_under` does not seem to accept targets specifying the current workspace:

```
$ bazel run //:run --run_under=@current//:wrapper
ERROR: Only a single target can be run. Your target pattern //:run expanded to the targets //:run, //:wrapper
```

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


```
--- BUILD.bazel
sh_binary(
    name = "run",
    srcs = ["run.sh"],
)

sh_binary(
    name = "wrapper",
    srcs = ["wrapper.sh"],
)

--- WORKSPACE.bazel
workspace(name = "current")

--- run.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "I ran"

--- wrapper.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "wrapping"
$@
echo "wrapped"
```

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


macOS 11.16

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


release 5.1.1

_No response_

_No response_

This similar issue: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7656
